{{Recipe}}

'''Abuk-abuk''' is a Malaysian steamed sweet dumpling made with sago. This version is made with white sugar, but gula melaka [[Cookbook:Palm Sugar|palm sugar]] is also used.

== Ingredients ==
* 120 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] [[Cookbook:Sago|sago]] pearls
* 100 g [[Cookbook:White Sugar|white granulated sugar]]
* 60 g grated [[Cookbook:Coconut|coconut]] meat
* ¼ [[Cookbook:Teaspoon|tsp]] [[Cookbook:Salt|salt]]
* ½ tsp green [[Cookbook:Food Coloring|food coloring]] (optional)
* 8 [[Cookbook:Each|ea.]] 2 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] pieces of [[Cookbook:Pandan|pandan]] leaf
* 8 [[Cookbook:Banana|banana leaves]], rolled into cones

== Procedure ==

# Prepare a [[Cookbook:Steamer|steamer]] over a few inches of simmering water.
# Place the sago in a [[Cookbook:Strainer|strainer]], and rinse well under running water. Let drain.
# Transfer the sago to a bowl, then mix in the coconut, salt, and food coloring.
# Fill each banana leaf cone with a scoop of the sago mixture. It should fill the cone about halfway.
# Place a scoop of sugar on top of the sago mixture.
# Top the sugar with another scoop of the sago mixture.
# Place a piece of pandan leaf on top of the sago mixture. Fold the banana leaf to fully enclose the packet.
# Transfer the packets to the steamer, cover, and [[Cookbook:Steaming|steam]] for 15–20 minutes.
# Remove from the steamer and allow to cool.
# Unwrap the packets and serve.
